question.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the denominator using $1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta :$

$$
\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta {cot}^{2}⁡\theta }{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }=\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta {cot}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }
$$

Next, we simplify by separating out the factors, and use the identity $\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta },$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta {cot}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot {cot}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }}{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }} \\  & =\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{\cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }}\cdot \frac{\cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }}{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{1}\cdot \frac{1}{1} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta {cot}^{2}⁡\theta }{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }=1
$$
